message.content:
It depends on what you’re looking for—genre, critical acclaim, audience reception, etc.—but here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated films from 2020:

| Rank | Title | Director | Genre | Notable Accolades |
|------|-------|----------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | *Parasite* (Korean) | Bong Joon‑ho | Thriller/Drama | Palme d’Or (Cannes), Best Picture Oscar |
| 2 | *1917* | Sam Mendes | War Drama | Best Cinematography & Visual Effects Oscars |
| 3 | *Soul* | Pete Docter | Animated/Fantasy | Best Animated Feature Oscar |
| 4 | *Tenet* | Christopher Nolan | Sci‑Fi Action | Nominated for 5 Oscars (no wins) |
| 5 | *The Trial of the Chicago 7* | Aaron Sorkin | Historical Drama | Golden Globe win for Best Original Screenplay |

If you’re into indie vibes, *Nomadland* (Chloé Zhao) and *Minari* (Lee Isaac Chung) were also critically lauded. For action lovers, *Extraction* (Chris Hemsworth) and *The Old Guard* (Charlize Theron) made waves.

**Bottom line:** If you want a film that won the biggest awards, *Parasite* is your pick. If you prefer a visually stunning war epic, go for *1917*. And if you’re after heartfelt storytelling with a touch of humor, *Soul* is a great choice.
